title: Is Groove GDPR Compliant? · Groove
text:
Short answer, YES. Long answer found below =)

## # We are GDPR ready and compliant

GDPR is the REGULATION (EU) 2016/679 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 27 April 2016 on the protection of natural persons with regard to the processing of personal data and on the free movement of such data, and repealing Directive 95/46/EC (General Data Protection Regulation).

## # 1. Data Protection Officer

Groove Networks LLC, 2 Dearborn St. Newport, RI United States is a data controller and a processor of personal data provided in Service.

Groove has its headquarters in the USA, which is why we have appointed a representative and internal data protection officer (“ DPO”) for you to contact if you have any questions or concerns about Groove’s personal data policies or practices.

You can reach out to our Data Protection Officer at dpo@groovehq.com.

## # 2. What do we do:

We provide a web application for help desk support. The main activity of Groove is gathering Your data from various channels (like email, twitter, facebook or widget you embed on your site - for a full list, see our Knowledge Base), grouping it, cross referencing and categorizing in order to make it accessible in the most user-friendly way, allowing you to deliver best possible support for your customers.

In order to perform our Service we process:

- (as a data controller) internet protocol (IP) of everyone who visits our service or if sending us a message name, email address and your general location (“Visitor”)
- (as a data controller) personal data of our customers (users of Service acting as Account Owner, Administrators, Agents - jointly referred to as (“You”));
- (as a processor on Your behalf ) personal data of Your customers.

...

Groove collects personal data (name, email) during registration process and when You add new Agents. Groove also collects personal data such as IP address and API token when You use our Service.

...

### # Your customer data

As a processor we do not collect any personal data without Your consent – we process Your customers’ personal data on Your behalf, which You have collected and explicitly provided to the Service. All this data belongs to You, we store it on our servers to support all of the Service’s features and remove them whenever You instruct us to.

We also provide You with features that enable You to profile Your customers by tracking their movements on the Knowledge Base (KB), by tracking read emails opened by Your customers as we also collect Your customers’ satisfaction ratings (for further information please visit Tracking and Profiling.

By using our contact form you can not only respond to your client’s message but also track your client’s movement on your website and collect data regarding your client’s location.

4. Internet protocol (IP);
5. API token;

7. General location

We collect information how You use our Service, i.e.

...

Where and to whom do we transfer Your data

In order to maintain and develop the Service Groove engages other entities. You gave us general written authorisation in the Data Processing Agreement.

...

## # 12. Cross-border US - EU transfer

Groove is established in the United States. Information we collect from You and on Your behalf will be processed in the United States.

Groove ensures that along with SCCs adequate safeguard have been adopted.

Groove also relays on derogations for specific situations as set forth in Article 49 of the GDPR. In particular, Groove collects and transfers to the U.S. personal data only: with Your consent; to perform a contract with You; or to fulfil a compelling legitimate interest of Groove in a manner that does not outweigh Your nor Your customers’ rights and freedoms (Using a Contact form).

Groove endeavours to apply suitable safeguards to protect the privacy and security of Your and Your customers’ personal data and to use it only consistent with Your relationship with Groove and the practices described in this Privacy Policy.

## # 13. Privacy Shield

Groove complies with the EU-U.S. Privacy Shield and the Swiss-U.S. Privacy Shield Frameworks as set forth by the U.S. Department of Commerce regarding the collection, use, and retention of personal information transferred from the European Union and/or Switzerland to the United States. Groove has certified to the Department of Commerce that it adheres to the Privacy Shield Principles. If there is any conflict between the terms in this privacy policy and the Privacy Shield Principles, the Privacy Shield Principles shall govern. To learn more about the Privacy Shield program, and to view our certification, please visit https://www.privacyshield.gov.

With respect to European Personal Data received or transferred pursuant to the Privacy Shield Framework, Groove is subject to the regulatory enforcement powers of the U.S. Federal Trade Commission. In certain situations, Groove may be required to disclose European Personal Data in response to lawful requests by public authorities, including meeting national security or law enforcement requirements.

Under certain conditions, more fully described on the Privacy Shield website, if you are an European resident, you may invoke binding arbitration when other dispute resolution procedures have been exhausted.

## # 14. Data storage

Groove stores Your and Your customers’ personal data on the servers of the cloud-based database management services Groove engages, located in the United States. Groove is hosted at AWS which announced compliance with GDPR. For more information on their servers and security, please see AWS security whitepaper https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/introduction-aws-security/welcome.html.

Full list of hosting providers can be found here.

Groove notifies You if we intend to change the list so You have the opportunity to object to such changes.

For more information regarding data storage contact our DPO at dpo@groovehq.com.

We keep all Your data that You have provided to us for the duration of Your business relationship with us and we remove data:

1) at Your explicit request (either via clicking the delete button next to a particular piece of data or via an email request to support@groovehq.com)

2) after You cancel Your account, at which point we remove Your data. This process takes up to 30 days to ensure all Your data is expunged from the system.

title: Groove GDPR: DPA, Data Role and Location
text:
Groove is a customer support tool. Most customers use it as a processor, it publishes its data processing agreement, and the data location depends on your account. Below: what to check and how to declare it.

...

The data usually involved: names, Email addresses, Account identifiers, Documents & attachments, Messages & support requests

...

Most customers use Groove as a processor: it handles personal data on their instructions, for the purposes they set. That is the common reading for customer support tools and it is what Privacyboard suggests.

As a processor, it needs a written agreement with you under Article 28, and you should know which subprocessors it uses. Confirm the role against your own agreement, because the way you use a tool can change it.

## Where does Groove store personal data?

Groove does not have one fixed location for every customer. The location depends on the plan, the account and the services you enable.

How to find yours: Check your account settings or Groove’s data processing terms for where your data is stored.

Even when the main location is in the EU, ask whether subprocessors or support access involve a transfer outside the EEA, and record it if so.

...

## Does Groove have a data processing agreement?

Checked on 1 November 2026. Vendors change their pages, so check the date.

Yes. Groove publishes the text of its data processing agreement on its own website. Article 28 of the GDPR requires a written contract with every processor, so this is the document to read and keep.

What we noted when we opened the page: Groove Data Processing Agreement (redirected from groovehq.com), last updated June 9, 2025. Processor is Groove Networks, LLC. No hosting region stated; permits transfer to the US with SCCs for EEA/Swiss data.

A page that exists does not mean you are covered. Whether the agreement applies to you depends on your plan and on what you accepted, so record the decision yourself in your vendor list.

## How to declare Groove

1. 1

### In your privacy policy

Name Groove as a recipient, say what it is used for (respond to customer enquiries and manage support conversations) and mention any transfer outside the EEA. Articles 13 and 14 ask you to tell people who receives their data.
2. 2

### In your vendor list

Add Groove with its purpose, the data involved, its role, its region and a link to the agreement. Privacyboard prefills all of this, you confirm or correct it.
3. 3

### In your processing register

Link Groove to the activities that use it, so each record shows its recipients. Article 30 asks the register to list the categories of recipients.

title: Groove HQ (groove.com) - Support Chat Widget & Consent Profile
text:
Groove HQ is a customer support helpdesk platform for small businesses. Scripts embed live chat widgets and support contact forms on websites, enabling real-time customer conversations. Collects visitor identifiers, chat transcripts, and browsing context; sets cookies to maintain chat session state.

## Is Groove HQ GDPR compliant?

Groove HQ typically loads functional trackers, which are not strictly necessary for your site to work. Under the GDPR and the ePrivacy Directive, non-essential cookies and trackers must stay blocked until a visitor gives clear opt-in consent. So Groove HQ can be fully GDPR compliant, but only if your site holds its scripts until consent is granted and lets visitors decline just as easily. Compliance depends on how your site loads Groove HQ, not on Groove HQ itself.

Consent required

Yes, block it until the visitor opts in

...

- Live chat widget: Renders a floating chat bubble (typically bottom-right) that expands into a real-time messaging interface, connecting visitors with support agents
- Contact form embedding: Displays support request forms that feed into Groove's shared inbox, collecting the visitor's name, email, and message
- Chat session cookies: Sets cookies to maintain the chat session across page navigations, so conversations persist as the visitor browses your site
- Visitor identification: Collects browser identifiers and browsing context (current page URL, referrer) to give support agents context about what the visitor is doing when they reach out
- Chat transcript storage: Records full chat transcripts and associates them with visitor contact information for follow-up and support history
- Availability detection: Checks agent availability in real-time to show online/offline status and switch between live chat and leave-a-message modes

...

## Consent & Compliance

Groove's chat widgets have a relatively contained compliance profile:

- GDPR: Chat transcripts and visitor contact information constitute personal data. Groove acts as a data processor, and a DPA should be in place. The visitor initiates the interaction, which supports a legitimate interest basis, but visitor identification cookies set before any interaction may need consent.
- ePrivacy Directive: Session cookies that maintain an active chat conversation are arguably strictly necessary for a service the visitor requested. However, cookies set preemptively (before the visitor opens the chat) for identification purposes may require consent.
- CCPA/CPRA: Visitor information collected through chat interactions should be disclosed in your privacy policy, including the fact that a third-party processor handles the data.

The compliance picture is cleaner when the widget only activates cookies after the visitor initiates a chat, rather than on page load.

title: Help desk software with EU data hosting (2026) · help-desk.reviews
text:
Freshdesk is the easiest help desk to host in the EU for customer support: you choose the EEA region at sign-up on any plan, and Freshworks publishes its sub-processor list. Zoho Desk offers EU data centres on every edition, including Free, and Jira Service Management lets Standard and Premium customers pin data to the EU on self-serve plans.

Every product here documents EU hosting, but how you get it differs: some let you pick at sign-up, some assign the region by your location, and some need a higher plan or a sales contract. Help Scout, second in our overall ranking, is absent because it hosts in the US only. EU hosting alone does not make a tool GDPR-compliant; see help desk data protection law and our rubric.

### Quick picks

- Self-serve EU hosting: Freshdesk — EEA region chosen at sign-up on any plan.
- EU hosting on a free plan: Zoho Desk — EU data centres on every edition, including Free.
- Internal IT: Jira Service Management — EU, German, UK and Swiss residency on Standard and above.
- Full omnichannel: Zendesk — Data Center Location add-on on Suite Professional.

...

Zoho Desk is a ticketing help desk with email, social and WhatsApp channels, a help centre and a chat widget, sold as part of the wider Zoho suite. Paid editions start at US$7 per user per month on annual billing, there is a free plan for up to 3 users, and the Zia AI assistant is included from the Professional edition at US$23. Zia AI Agents come with a free monthly token allowance, but the price of usage beyond it is not published.

EU data centres are available on every edition, including Free, and the data centre follows the country chosen at sign-up.

...

## How to choose

If you want EU hosting without talking to sales, pick Freshdesk and select the EEA region when you create the account, or Zoho Desk, whose EU data centre follows the country you sign up from.

If you run an internal IT desk and need data pinned to Germany or the EU, pick Jira Service Management Standard or above.

If you are on HubSpot's CRM, HubSpot Service Hub hosts paid accounts in Germany, but only paid ones; a free-only account stays in the US.

If you need every channel and are on Zendesk already, activate the Data Center Location add-on on Suite Professional; on Suite Team you would have to upgrade to US$115 per agent first. Compare Zendesk vs Freshdesk.

If you are considering Intercom or Front, plan for a sales conversation: Intercom's EU region needs a new workspace on a sales contract, and Front sets up EEA hosting on request.

## Verdict

Freshdesk is our default for EU-hosted customer support: self-serve EEA hosting on any plan and the strongest data-protection record on this list. Ignore it if you run an internal IT desk (pick Jira Service Management) or need a free plan (pick Zoho Desk).

## For buyers in the United Kingdom

A help desk holds your customers' personal data, so UK GDPR requires a written contract with the vendor. Hosting outside the UK, including in the EU, is a restricted transfer that needs its own safeguard. And since 19 June 2026 you must let people complain about how you use their data and acknowledge each complaint within 30 days.

...

Does EU hosting make a help desk GDPR-compliant?

No. EU hosting reduces transfers, but you still need a data processing agreement, a sub-processor list you can check, and a lawful basis for any transfer by support staff or AI providers outside the EU. Our guide to help desk data protection law explains what to check.

GDPR governs how personal data of EU residents is handled. It does not ban storing data outside the EU, but it sets strict conditions on transfers and requires a lawful basis plus safeguards. Tickets, chat transcripts, and contact details all count as personal data.

## What to verify before signing

Before you commit, get these in writing:

- The specific data center location. "EU hosting" should map to a named region (Frankfurt or Amsterdam, say), not a vague claim. Ask which country, and on which plan.
- The sub-processor list. Even an EU-hosted tool may route data through US-based sub-processors for analytics, email, or AI. Request the list and check where each one sits.
- Where AI prompts go. AI features often send prompts to a model provider outside the EU. Confirm whether AI processing happens in the EU, especially for tickets or KB content.
- DPA availability. A Data Processing Agreement is standard for GDPR. Make sure the vendor offers one and check which transfer mechanisms (SCCs, DPF) it relies on.
- Plan gating. Confirm whether EU residency is included by default or needs a specific plan or paid add-on, so there are no surprises at renewal.
